subject: "Error in while (maxStepsL > 0 & !is.nan(lp) & lp >= u) {" when using customized function

messages.author: 6d330da989c91221
messages.subject: "Error in while (maxStepsL > 0 & !is.nan(lp) & lp >= u) {" when using customized function
parts:
Hi! I am a beginner in Nimble. I want to fit a model that represents transmission of a pathogen. I tried to fit a model with Nimble to simulated data, but repeatedly encountered the following error message:


warning: logProb of data node y.obs[1, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[2, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[3, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[4, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[5, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[6, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[7, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[8, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[9, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[10, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[11, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
warning: logProb of data node y.obs[12, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.
Error in while (maxStepsL > 0 & !is.nan(lp) & lp >= u) { : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: There were 12 warnings (use warnings() to see them)

> warnings()
Warning messages:
1: In dbinom(x, size, prob, log) : NaNs produced
2: In dbinom(x, size, prob, log) : NaNs produced
...


The code for simulating data and Nimble model is:


require(nimble)

## Parameters for simulation
lmd.0 <- 1      # rate of appearance of initial cases
b0 <- 1         # transmission probability
a0 <- .7        # detection probability
N <- 12         # no. of cells
t.max <- 10     # no. of days
popul <- 100    # population size of each cell
n.seed <- 1     # seed to use

## Simulation
lmd <- matrix(0, N, t.max)
p <- matrix(0, N, t.max)
y <- array(0, c(N, t.max, 1)) # no. of cases per cell and day
y.obs <- array(0, c(N, t.max, 1)) # no. of observed cases per cell and day
set.seed(n.seed)
for (i in 1:N) { # initialization for t = 1
  y[i,1,1] <- rpois(1, lmd.0)
  y.obs[i,1,1] ~ rbinom(1, y[i,1,1], a0)
}
for(t in 2:t.max){
  for (i in 1:N) {
    lmd[i,t] <- b0 * (y[i,t-1,1] / popul)
    p[i,t] <- 1 - exp(-lmd[i,t])
    y[i,t,1] <- rbinom(1, popul, p[i,t])
    y.obs[i,t,1] <- rbinom(1, y[i,t,1], a0)
  }
}

## Customized distributions for Nimble
dbinomCond <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0), size = double(0), prob = double(0),
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    if(x > size){
      if(log == 1) return(-400) # '-400' is just an arbitrarily low value
      else return(exp(-400))
    } else return(dbinom(x, size, prob, log))
  })
rbinomCond <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n = integer(0), size = double(0), prob = double(0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    if(n != 1) print("rbinomCond only allows n = 1; using n = 1.")
    return(rbinom(1, size, prob))
  })

## Nimble model
prbCode <- nimbleCode(
  {
    for (i in 1:N) {
      y[i,1] ~ dpois(lmd.0)
      y.obs[i,1] ~ dbinomCond(a0, y[i,1])
      # y.obs[i,1] ~ dbinom(a0, y[i,1])
    }
    for(t in 2:t.max){
      for (i in 1:N) {
        log(lmd[i,t]) <- b0 * (y[i,t-1] / popul)
        p[i,t] <- 1 - exp(-lmd[i,t])
        y[i,t] ~ dbinom(p[i,t], popul)
        y.obs[i,t] ~ dbinomCond(size = y[i,t], prob = a0)
        # y.obs[i,t] ~ dbinom(a0, y[i,t])
      }
    }
    lmd.0 ~ dgamma(3,2)
    a0 ~ dbeta(5,3)
    b0 ~ dbeta(5,1)
  }
)

## Additional elements for Nimble
prbInits <- function() list(lmd.0 = rgamma(1,3,2), b0 = rbeta(1,5,1), a0 = rbeta(1,5,3))
prbConsts <- list(N=N,t.max=t.max,popul=popul)
prbData <- list(y.obs=y.obs[,,1])
set.seed(n.seed)
prb <- nimbleModel(code = prbCode, name = "prb", constants = prbConsts,
                   data = prbData, inits = prbInits())
prbConf <- configureMCMC(prb, print = FALSE)
prbMCMC <- buildMCMC(prbConf)

## Run Nimble model
prbMCMC$run(niter = 10) # 'niter' is low for fitting, but enough to show errors

(I’ve used a customized distribution for the likelihood because in the eventual real data it is likely to have false positives, alike in the current simulated data.)

 

If ‘dbinom’ is used for the likelihood (currently commented), instead of ‘dbindomCond’, the model runs but the resulting estimates are very different from the actual ones and, in fact, the posteriors do not converge.


So, the obvious question is what to do about these errors.


Thanks!

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: "Error in while (maxStepsL > 0 & !is.nan(lp) & lp >= u) {" when using customized function
parts:
Hi Juan,

It looks like in your first declaration with dbinomCond, you have the arguments in the wrong order.

Here is some code I used after building your model to isolate the problem:

prb$calculate()
## There is an error that looks like it's from code inside dBinomCond.
## Often, this means something is not initialized well or for some other reason arguments are not sensible.
## I will try simulating and calculating the whole model.
prb$simulate()
prb$calculate()
warnings()
## There are errors in some dbinom calls. Try
## to determine which ones.
prb$calculate("y") ## ok
prb$calculate("y.obs[,1]") ## problem is here
prb$calculate("y.obs[,2:10]") ## ok

-Perry
